First public release of **Soundstave** – spectral analysis of recordings, automatic note
detection, note editing on top of the spectrogram, and export to MIDI and MusicXML.

*Første offentlige udgave af Soundstave: spektralanalyse af lydoptagelser, automatisk
tonegenkendelse, redigering af noder direkte i spektrogrammet og eksport til MIDI og MusicXML.
Brugerfladen er på dansk.*

## Highlights

- **Import** WAV, FLAC, AIFF and MP3 (open or drag-and-drop).
- **High-resolution spectrogram** on a note-aligned logarithmic pitch axis, with keyboard,
  waveform and a piano-roll grid layer – all synchronised for zoom, scrolling and playback.
- **Polyphonic note detection** in the background (with progress and cancel) that keeps
  overtones out, separates repeated notes and estimates velocity.
- **Tempo and beat detection** directly from the audio, so the grid lines up with a freely
  played recording.
- **Editing**: select, move, resize, draw, split, merge, delete, copy/paste, transpose,
  snap to 1/4 … 1/32 or triplets – everything undoable.
- **Playback** of the recording and the MIDI notes, separately or together, with a built-in
  instrument, and **sample-accurate looping** of a section.
- **Export** to Standard MIDI File and to readable MusicXML (bars, ties, chords, voices,
  grand staff) with a quantization preview – opens in MuseScore, Dorico and Sibelius.
- **Projects** (`.soundstave`) remember notes, tempo, view, loop and settings; you are asked
  to save before closing.

See the [README](https://github.com/shenphenchoedron-hue/Soundstave#readme) for mouse and
keyboard controls.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Linux (x86-64) | `Soundstave-0.2.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` – unpack and run `Soundstave` (needs ALSA, X11, FreeType) |
| Windows (64-bit) | `Soundstave-0.2.0-windows-x64.zip` – unpack and run `Soundstave.exe` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `Soundstave-0.2.0-macos-universal.zip` – the app is not signed: right-click → *Open* the first time |

The Windows and macOS builds are made and tested automatically by GitHub Actions; they have not
yet been tried by hand on those systems.

## Known limitations

- Note detection is signal-processing based; dense mixes with drums or heavy reverb need more
  manual correction.
- One tempo per project; key signature is always C major.
